name: Koalas have human-like fingerprints

hook_variants.template: Not a human. But the fingerprints say otherwise.
What animal has fingerprints almost identical to yours?
Someone once feared koala prints could be found at crime scenes.

sections.text: Koalas have fingerprints so similar to humans that experts once mistook them for human prints.
They're the only non-primates with friction-ridge fingerprints like ours.
sections.subtitle: only non-primate with human-like prints

sections.text: They even have similar ridge patterns and whorls — developed independently, since they last shared an ancestor ~70 million years ago.
sections.title: convergence

sections.text: One case almost sent koala prints to a crime lab as evidence before the mix-up was caught.
sections.title: the story
sections.body: an actual police mix-up, by a fingerprint expert's claim

sections.text: Criminology joke aside: same skin ridges, totally different tree-climbing reasons.
Follow for more doppelgangers in nature.

facts.claim: Koalas have fingerprints very similar to human fingerprints, a case of convergent evolution
Koalas are one of the few non-primate mammals with friction-ridge fingerprints
Marsupials and primates last shared a common ancestor roughly 70 million years ago

titles: The animal that could commit your crimes
